name: llmc_trimat_forward
goal: Port trimat_forward_harness.cu (llm.c dev/cuda/trimat_forward.cu, fp32 build) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers. Keep every kernel variant k in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] as its own SYCL kernel, computed on the SYCL device, and keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <input> <output> B T C NH` reads the inputs and writes each variant's outputs in order as raw float32, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output (atol 0.0001 + rtol FLT_EPSILON*|ref|, llm.c's own fp32 rule). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: migrate's output under migrated/ counts, so delete it (delete_file) once your own port is done. migrate's output can be long: read it in parts (read_file offset/limit) or work from the CUDA harness. cuBLAS calls go to oneMath (oneapi::math::blas, #include <oneapi/math.hpp>; the compile flags already link -lonemath), not to oneapi::mkl product APIs.

museport.note: B=2, T=256 (llm.c: B=8, T=1024); C=768, NH=12 (HS=64) as in llm.c. T=256 keeps T%128==0 assert and gives 2x2 tiles per head to cover diagonal and off-diagonal blocks.

reference.kind: differential: the original CUDA's recorded output
